The Draw of a Cluster Replicate Beside Random Effects

Source: R/bootstrap_cluster_random.R
boot_cluster_random_plan.Rd

Returns the function of bootstrap_plan() for a cluster bootstrap of a fit with modelterms7::random() terms. A draw is the vector of the clusters drawn, and the attribute build of the result turns a draw into the specification of the replicate.

Usage

boot_cluster_random_plan(object, resample, spec0, design0)

Arguments

object

The StatmodFit().

resample

A ClusterResample.

spec0, design0

Its specification and design.

Value

A function of no arguments returning a list with pick, with attributes kind ("regrouped"), targets, random and build.

Details

The clusters are drawn with replacement, \(G\) of \(G\). A cluster drawn \(k\) times enters the replicate \(k\) times, once for each draw, and each copy is a new cluster. The grouping variable of every random-effect term is relabeled in the replicate so that the groups of two copies are different groups, each with an effect of its own, as in Stata's bootstrap, cluster() idcluster(). A group is relabeled when every one of its observations lies in a single cluster; a group that spans several clusters keeps its label, and its effect is shared by the copies.

The design of the replicate is rebuilt on the rows drawn. The terms other than the random-effect terms are reapplied with modelterms7::term_predict(), so a basis keeps the knots of the fit and a factor its contrasts. A random effect term is built again with modelterms7::term_build() on the relabeled groups; its hyperparameters are those of the fit. The weights, the offsets and the response are those of the rows drawn.

The coordinates that a replicate has in common with the fit are those of the terms that are not random effects. build() returns their positions in the replicate (map, with NA for a coordinate of the fit that has no counterpart), the starting values of the replicate, and expand(), which returns the coefficients of a refit in the stacked positions of the fit with NA at the random effects. A draw that does not reproduce the design of the fit when every cluster is drawn once is an error: it means that a variable of the model is not a column of the data.
